summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to deposit high-k dielectrics (Al2O3 and HfO2) onto functionalized suspended single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs). The functionalization with -NO2 groups made the SWNTs reactive with ALD precursors, enabling conformal coating. The ALD process was performed at 225°C, and the deposited oxides helped anchor the SWNTs to the substrate, preventing lateral motion during subsequent chemical treatments. The functionalization and ALD steps were shown to be reversible, with the functionalization affecting the electrical properties of the SWNTs, which could be partially recovered through annealing.
evidence: The metal sources used for Al2O3 and HfO2 were trimethylaluminum and tetrakis(diethylamino)hafnium, respectively. H2O was used as the oxygen source for both materials, and 225°C was the deposition temperature used in both cases. The purpose of this ALD step was twofold. While it left the main body of the suspended nanotubes bare, it helped to anchor them to the supporting substrate by growing up and around the segments that were in contact with the Si3N4 membrane. The fact that the SWNTs were suspended over a gap made them ideal structures for transmission electron microscopy (TEM) studies. The IV curve of the as-grown SWNT is slightly nonlinear, corresponding to a nanotube with semiconducting properties. The conductance of the as-grown SWNTs after 10 nm HfO2 deposition increases. Chemical functionalization caused a dramatic resistance increase. Anneals in an inert argon atmosphere were performed to achieve complete ligand cleavage along the entire nanotube length, effectively restoring the SWNT to its original hybridization state and corresponding conductive properties.
